vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — one point down from last night's close of 5. The step back is driven by three distinct overnight developments, none of which individually collapses the positive signal from yesterday but together represent a measurable degradation. First: Washington Post confirmed US forces struck two Iranian-flagged tankers in the Strait overnight — active kinetics during the Project Freedom pause. The pause has not produced a kinetic freeze; IRGC naval assets continue operating against US and commercial assets in the Strait. Any US casualty or vessel loss during the pause would immediately trigger pressure for resumption of Project Freedom 'at a much higher level.' Second: Al Jazeera's May 9 morning liveblog logged Israeli air strikes on Lebanon — a new theater that signals regional conflict expansion beyond the Iran-US bilateral frame. Lebanon adds IRGC proxy activation risk, European refugee pressure, and a second NATO-relevant front simultaneously with the Hormuz crisis. Third: Iran's MOU non-response is now 90+ hours past the 48-hour window — each day of non-response consumes diplomatic credibility and narrows the Iranian executive track's ability to claim it is 'reviewing' rather than refusing. The market has already begun pricing this: Brent's rebound to $101.73 on May 8 close confirms deal-delay repricing, not deal-imminent. The CIT Section 122 tariff ruling is a fourth signal: narrow injunction (plaintiff-limited), but it establishes the legal challenge architecture that could erode Warsh's inherited tariff landscape before his first FOMC in June. Against all this: the April jobs beat (177K NFP, 4.2% UR) from Friday gives the economic picture a genuine floor. Warsh's vote is scheduled for Monday. CISA reports no IRGC destructive cyberattack through Day 6 post-Project Freedom. Canvas is criminal, not state-sponsored. Vibe 4 is the right call: structurally worse than yesterday's 5, but not yet at the 3-level degradation that would signal deal collapse or imminent Project Freedom resumption.

items.headline: US Strikes Two Iranian-Flagged Tankers Overnight; Active Kinetics Continue During Project Freedom Pause
items.summary: The Washington Post reported overnight that US forces struck two Iranian-flagged tankers in or near the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating tensions, despite the ostensible Project Freedom pause (Pause Day 4). The strikes are characterized as responsive to Iranian attacks on US naval vessels — consistent with CENTCOM's declared self-defense doctrine. The incident confirms the Project Freedom pause is not a kinetic freeze: IRGC naval assets continue to engage US forces and potentially commercial shipping. The dual-track dynamic — Foreign Ministry 'reviewing' while IRGC units attack — is either deliberate pressure maximization or fragmented IRGC command coherence during a negotiating period. Operationally, the distinction matters less than the fact of sustained attacks during an ostensible pause. Trump has not announced a resumption of Project Freedom. Any Iranian attack resulting in US casualties or a vessel loss during the pause creates immediate domestic and operational pressure for resumption 'at a much higher level.' Commercial transit remains suspended pending escort mission resumption; approximately 1,600 ships and 23,000 sailors remain stranded in or near the Strait.

items.headline: Israel Air Strikes Lebanon: New Secondary Theater Opens on Europe Day; IRGC Proxy Dynamics Activated
items.summary: Al Jazeera's May 9 morning liveblog reported Israeli air strikes on Lebanon, adding a new secondary theater to the regional conflict architecture defined since February 28 by the Iran-US Hormuz confrontation. The Israel-Lebanon front introduces compounding variables: IRGC proxy activation risk (Hezbollah is both a Lebanon-resident actor and an IRGC affiliate whose operational status affects the Iran-US negotiating dynamic); European political pressure on a day — May 9, Europe Day — when the EU is simultaneously managing Russia-Ukraine, US-EU trade tensions (Trump threatening EU auto tariffs from 15% to 25%), and China trade friction alongside the Hormuz crisis. The Lebanon front's direct relevance to the MOU timeline is indirect but real: IRGC proxy escalation in Lebanon complicates a deal that asks Iran to accept restraint while its regional proxy architecture is simultaneously being degraded. Hezbollah capacity is reduced from 2024–2025 Israeli degradation campaigns, limiting scale; but the opening of this front is a directional negative for the diplomacy window. No US involvement in Lebanon operations has been confirmed.

items.headline: Iran MOU Non-Response 90+ Hours; Executive-Parliament Divergence Structural; Pakistan Channel Active; Expediency Council Demands Reparations
items.summary: Iran's formal response to the 14-point MOU framework transmitted via Pakistan and Oman channels remains absent as of Saturday morning — approximately 90 hours past the 48-hour response window that expired May 8. FM Baqaei's last public statement: 'reviewing.' Parliament's Foreign Policy Committee spokesperson Rezaei called it 'an American wish list'; Speaker Ghalibaf posted 'Operation Fauxios' mockery on social media. Neither the parliament nor Ghalibaf has authority to accept or reject the deal — that remains with Khamenei and the executive track. The Expediency Council has raised a reparations demand as a condition. The structural ambiguity is this: the deal has not been rejected by the authority that would accept or reject it — Khamenei — but the parliament, Expediency Council, and IRGC each have domestic-audience incentives to resist acceptance under conditions that resemble coercion. Pakistan's intermediary channel remains active; no Pakistan Foreign Ministry statement has confirmed receipt of a formal Iranian response. France's multinational Strait security architecture (proposed by Macron) remains a potential face-saving vehicle. Times of Israel earlier confirmed Saudi Arabia denied US airspace for Hormuz operations — a continuing operational constraint that limits US kinetic escalation options if the MOU is rejected.

items.headline: CIT Strikes Down Section 122 Tariffs: 10% Surcharge on $1.2T of Imports Invalidated as to Plaintiffs; Injunction Not Nationwide; Appeal Architecture Active
items.summary: The US Court of International Trade issued a ruling May 7, 2026 — now spreading through trade counsel networks and supply chain planning teams Saturday morning — invalidating the Trump administration's Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 tariff as applied to plaintiff importers. Background: after SCOTUS ruled 6-3 in February 2026 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, the administration pivoted to Section 122, imposing a 10% ad valorem surcharge on approximately $1.2T (34%) of annual imports effective February 24, 2026, scheduled to expire after 150 days (July 24, 2026). The CIT held that the administration's metrics — current account balance and goods trade deficits — did not constitute 'balance-of-payments deficits' as Congress defined the term in 1974. The court entered a permanent injunction against collection from plaintiff importers only; it explicitly declined to enter a nationwide injunction. For Warsh's incoming policy environment: the CIT ruling creates legal uncertainty about the durability of the 11.8% average effective US tariff rate. If the Federal Circuit appeal accelerates before his first FOMC (June 16–17), the tariff structure Warsh inherits on Monday may be materially altered by June. Immediate business impact: plaintiff importers may stop duty payment pending appeal; all other importers must continue paying unless they file separately. Moody's Analytics chief economist Zandi assessed tariffs as having done 'significant damage to the US economy' — Canada and Mexico's markets outperformed the S&P 500 by 28.93 and 25.17 percentage points respectively over the past year.

items.headline: ShinyHunters Breaches Instructure/Canvas: 3.6TB Data, 9,000 Schools Including WWU, Ransomware Demand; Largest Education Breach of 2026
items.summary: The cybercrime group ShinyHunters claimed responsibility May 7–8, 2026 for a breach of Instructure, the company behind the Canvas learning management system used by approximately 9,000 schools and universities nationwide. The group claims to have extracted 3.6 terabytes of data and issued a ransom demand. Canvas, which serves an estimated 30 million students and educators, was taken offline for portions of the breach period — creating significant disruption to coursework, grade submission, and finals preparation. Western Washington University (Bellingham, WA) was among the confirmed affected PNW institutions. The breach is a criminal extortion incident, not a state-sponsored critical infrastructure attack in the CISA AA26-097A threat class (Iranian-affiliated PLCs, water/energy/government sectors). However, the scale — 3.6TB, 9,000 institutions, likely including financial aid and student records — makes it operationally significant and a potential vector for downstream credential-based attacks. The breach was still unresolved as of May 8 per The Front Online reporting. This is not a CISA advisory-level event but it is the most significant US cyber incident of the week — and its education-sector concentration at finals week represents maximum institutional disruption timing.

items.headline: CISA Day 6: No IRGC Destructive Attack Confirmed; Overnight Tanker Strikes Elevate Weekend Risk Window; CI Fortify Operative
items.summary: Six days after Project Freedom launched (May 4), CISA has confirmed no IRGC-affiliated or Handala-attributed destructive cyberattack on US critical infrastructure. The sustained absence is a material positive — every day without a destructive IRGC cyber operation is a day of operational continuity for water utilities, energy operators, and transportation entities already planning 'weeks to months' in isolation mode per CI Fortify guidance. However, the overnight tanker strikes — US forces hitting two Iranian-flagged vessels in the Strait — represent a new IRGC provocation event that could internally justify a calibrated cyber response during the nominal pause. Weekend staffing reductions across IT security teams compound the timing risk: reduced incident response capacity Saturday–Sunday is a structural vulnerability that threat actors have historically exploited. CISA has issued no updated advisory beyond AA26-097A (April 7, 2026). NERC continues active grid monitoring. FINRA financial-sector alert remains in effect. The Canvas/ShinyHunters breach demonstrates that weekend timing of significant cyber operations against major platforms remains a preferred pattern regardless of state affiliation. No confirmed US critical infrastructure disruption has been attributed to Iranian actors through the morning of May 9.

items.headline: Triple-Convergence Week Opens Monday: Warsh May 11 5:30 PM Vote, Reconciliation Deadline May 15, Powell Expiry May 15; WPA Day 10 Unresolved
items.summary: Monday May 11 marks the formal opening of the highest-density institutional convergence week of the 119th Congress's second session. The Senate is scheduled to vote on Kevin Warsh's Federal Reserve Chair nomination at 5:30 PM ET — before Jerome Powell's May 15 statutory term expiration. Warsh's confirmation path is solid: 53 Republican Senate seats plus Fetterman's indicated support provides a working margin of approximately 54–46. Warsh's inherited environment as of Monday: UR 4.2%, Brent $101.73, PCE 3.5%, federal funds rate 3.50–3.75%, Section 122 tariff architecture under CIT legal challenge. Reconciliation 2.0: all designated Senate committees must submit measures to the Budget Committee by May 15. The Senate Homeland Security and Judiciary committees' $72B ICE/CBP package was CBO-scored May 4; remaining committees face a 6-day deadline from Monday. The $1B White House ballroom security earmark (disclosed NPR May 6) remains in the bill unresolved. WPA Day 10 past April 29 statutory deadline: the constitutional accountability gap — 36+ hours of offensive operations without congressional authorization — persists and widens. All six Senate war-powers resolutions attempted so far have failed. Project Freedom's pause provides temporary political relief but the WPA issue has not been resolved.

items.headline: DOGE: White House Asks Congress to Codify USAID/CPB Cuts; Peace Corps Meeting Today; July 4 Expiration 56 Days Out; SCOTUS Mass-Layoff Request Pending
items.summary: The White House formally asked Congress this week to codify DOGE-implemented cuts to USAID and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting — a codification request that acknowledges the legal fragility of executive-branch-only DOGE cuts ahead of the July 4 statutory expiration. DOGE staff are scheduled to meet with Peace Corps officials today (Saturday May 9), continuing the department's review of agencies targeted for elimination or restructuring. The DOGE July 4 expiration is now 56 days out. A Brookings Institution budget expert estimated DOGE's total savings at approximately $20 billion — well below stated targets — with the bulk from international funding and minority program cuts rather than structural government reform. A federal judge separately ruled that $100M+ in NEH grant cuts were discriminatory. The SCOTUS emergency application authorizing the mass federal layoff plan (estimated 300,000 positions) remains pending with no ruling timeline. Authorization before July 4 would provide legal cover for remaining DOGE structural cuts before statutory expiration. The CIT's Section 122 tariff invalidation adds a parallel legal-challenge precedent that may energize litigation against other executive-authority-reliant DOGE actions.

items.headline: Oregon Fire Season Day 2 Active; Portland 88°F Today, 90°F Sunday; 400+ PNW Communities at Higher-Than-Mapped Risk; Super El Niño Potential; 23 Days to Above-Normal East Cascades Onset
items.summary: Oregon's 2026 fire season, declared effective 12:01 AM PDT May 8, is now active Day 2 with 700 ODF wildland firefighters and 300 fire trucks in protective position for 16 million Oregon acres, supplemented by 300+ local fire departments and federal and tribal wildland fire resources. Portland's weekend forecast: 88°F Saturday, 90°F Sunday May 10. The 90°F threshold drives accelerated soil moisture depletion and fine-fuel curing in the Columbia Gorge and east of the Cascades — 23 days ahead of the June 1 above-normal fire risk onset for eastern Oregon. No NWS Portland red flag warning issued as of Saturday morning; east-gradient wind potential in the Columbia Gorge is being monitored through Sunday. A new wildfire community risk assessment (The News Guard) identified 400+ PNW communities at higher risk than previously mapped. Elevated-risk communities include Oregon towns Cave Junction, La Pine, and Glendale; Washington towns Selah, White Salmon, and Ellensburg. FOX 13 Seattle reports a potential super El Niño formation that could raise the upper-tail wildfire risk scenario for Washington beyond the already-elevated ECMWF May–July baseline (well-below-normal precipitation, well-above-normal temperatures, deepest PNW precipitation deficits in the lower 48). Oregon's fire season is projected to extend through October — approximately one month beyond historical average. Oregon's 2025–2026 winter was tied with 1934 as the warmest on record. AccuWeather projects 5.5 million acres burned nationally in 2026. The DOGE-related elimination of Forest Service regional fire science capacity continues to degrade the pre-positioning modeling that ODF crews rely on for risk-weighted placement decisions.

items.headline: PNW Measles: OHA Wastewater Active in Non-Reporting Counties; Count Update Expected Monday–Tuesday; WA 40+; Catch-Up Window 5–6 Weeks; Canvas Disruption Secondary Complication
items.summary: No new Oregon Health Authority case count was published Friday or Saturday — the most recent published figure remains 20 confirmed cases as of April 22, 2026, which OHA officials have characterized as substantially understated. OHA's wastewater surveillance dashboard continues to detect measles viral concentrations in counties with no confirmed cases, a leading indicator of transmission outpacing case-finding capacity. Washington State holds at 40+ confirmed cases across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in formal outbreak status. National total as of April 30, 2026: 1,814 confirmed cases across 37 jurisdictions. The structural context is unchanged: below-threshold MMR vaccination coverage in pockets of both states, DOGE-related CDC response capacity constraints, and active school-year community spread dynamics. The school-year catch-up window (most PNW districts end mid-to-late June) is approximately 5–6 weeks remaining. Secondary complication: the Canvas/ShinyHunters breach (9,000 institutions offline May 7–8) disrupted LMS-dependent health communications and school nurse messaging at affected PNW campuses for the weekend period. Next expected OHA case count: Monday–Tuesday, consistent with OHA's weekday publishing cadence. The published count is expected to show a material increase from April 22's 20-case figure given sustained wastewater detection in non-reporting counties.
